v4.9.083 - a hand on the page holds the fetching back (#371)

#371 Roman, after watching me fail at this three times: "a device you write on in
     scribble does not need to pull new stuff from the server while your pen is
     down... and maybe pause loading for five seconds after the last stroke."

     That is the fix, and it is better than any of mine.

     THE FAULT: fetching is what rebuilds the page, and rebuilding the 3x2 page
     throws away the whole scribble layer and makes a new one. A sync landing
     mid-stroke destroyed the canvas under the hand: the half-made mark went with
     it and the finger came up on an element that no longer existed. Drawing fast
     simply means more strokes are in progress when a sync arrives.

     WHY MY THREE ATTEMPTS FAILED: all of them held back the REDRAW - first the
     layer, then the page, then the whole redraw - and every one tore the screen.
     The layer ended up not rebuilt at all, or rebuilt from notes taken before
     the person had finished.

     Holding back the FETCH costs nothing. Nothing is torn down, nothing goes
     stale. The work is still on the server, the heartbeat comes round every few
     seconds, and it lands the moment the hand is off.

     The five seconds matter as much as the stroke: a series of quick marks has
     gaps between them, and a rebuild landing in one of those gaps is the same
     interruption. Applies to the scribble layer and to drawing on a version,
     since both already say when a stroke is in progress.

     The test that describes this failed three times against my attempts and was
     parked. It is back in, and green.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ON THE LIST

Scribble batching was only ever the cheap route to this. With the fetching held
it is no longer a correctness question, only traffic: a fast hand still sends one
push per stroke, but nothing comes back to disturb it. Demoted.

28 of 28 pass, with the local server staying up.
